oil.summary: Crude markets remain in full risk-premium mode. Brent settled above $93/bbl (+3.1% today, +20.4% on the month) after reports of Iran striking oil tankers in an escalating Hormuz campaign, with the strait's effective disruption forcing Asian refiners to scramble for alternative August cargoes. WTI followed at $86.44 (+1.8%), also supported by Trump's vow of retaliation following the killing of three US soldiers. India is pivoting toward Russian crude as Iranian barrels disappear; Pakistan is canvassing US, Nigerian, and Central Asian suppliers. The divergence in refined products is notable: RBOB gasoline fell 4.7% on the session despite crude strength, while heating oil shed 1.9% but remains up 30.9% on the month, consistent with distillate-supply anxiety. A 2-million-barrel US crude inventory build (EIA, week ending July 17) provided modest relief but was insufficient to cap the geopolitical bid.
drivers: Iran-Hormuz escalation: tanker attacks and strait disruption removing Middle East barrels from global supply, lifting Brent decisively above $90
Demand-side rerouting: India boosting Russian crude imports; Pakistan seeking US/West African alternatives, tightening Atlantic Basin differentials
Bearish offset: EIA reported a 2-million-barrel US crude inventory build for the week ending July 17, capping further upside in WTI

gas.summary: European gas prices surged to €62.40/MWh on TTF (+4.6% today, +49% in a month), driven by a combustible mix of geopolitical supply disruption and alarming storage data. Equinor CEO Anders Opedal warned that European storage is unlikely to reach even 80% fill before winter, the weakest pre-winter cushion in 15 years. The Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb closures are simultaneously squeezing LNG availability, pushing buyers toward coal and oil as substitutes—a stark reversal of decarbonization trends. Equinor itself reported a 93% Q2 profit surge on the back of surging oil and gas prices. Henry Hub was comparatively subdued at $2.945/MMBtu (+2.8% today), down 9.5% on the month, reflecting a still-ample North American supply backdrop that sharply contrasts with European tightness.
drivers: European storage deficit: Equinor CEO flagged sub-80% fill probability before winter, the worst position in 15 years, underpinning the TTF rally
LNG supply squeeze: Hormuz and Bab el-Mandeb disruptions curtailing Middle East LNG flows, forcing buyers toward coal and oil substitution
Henry Hub divergence: US prices down 9.5% on the month, insulated by domestic supply adequacy, highlighting a widening transatlantic gas market split

power.summary: Power and carbon markets moved in lockstep with the broader fossil-fuel complex. EU carbon allowances (EUA) rose 4.0% to $81.77, consistent with higher gas-fired generation costs and fuel-switching incentives pulling coal back into the merit order. Japan's day-ahead spot electricity prices reached a 3.5-year high, driven by soaring fuel costs, heat waves, and a weakening yen. GE Vernova raised its full-year revenue outlook on surging demand for gas turbines and grid equipment—AI data-centre load growth providing durable structural support even as wind remained weak. The headline flow was thinner in power-specific news today, but the through-line is clear: the Hormuz-driven LNG and oil price shock is transmitting directly into power costs across Asia and Europe, with carbon pricing amplifying the signal for European utilities.
drivers: EUA rally (+4% today): higher gas input costs and coal re-entry into the generation mix are lifting carbon prices in tandem with TTF
Japan power prices at 3.5-year high: surging fuel costs and heat-wave demand combining with yen weakness to pressure spot electricity markets
GE Vernova guidance lift: AI-driven data-centre load growth fuelling sustained demand for gas turbines and grid infrastructure, reinforcing the gas-power nexus
